📌 Fake Migration Sites: When "Upgrade Now" Is the Scam

Main Points
⏺ Protocols regularly retire old contracts, bridges and token versions
⏺ Scammers copy these announcements and push look-alike "migration" or "claim" pages
⏺ This post explains how the trap works and how to check a link

1️⃣ Core Idea — When a project announces an upgrade, deprecation or claim deadline, fake sites appear that look identical to the real app and ask you to "migrate" or "claim before it's too late".
2️⃣ Why It Happens — A real deadline creates urgency. People search for the page, click an ad or a link in a reply, and connect their wallet without checking the address bar.
3️⃣ Example — A project says old contracts will be paused next month. A reply under the post links to a "migration portal". It asks you to sign an approval — and that signature lets the attacker move your tokens.
4️⃣ Red Flags — Links from replies, DMs or search ads, a domain that differs by one letter, requests for your seed phrase, and "unlimited" token approvals for a simple migration.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — Open migration and claim pages only from the project's official site or documentation, bookmark them, read what you are signing, and revoke approvals you no longer need.

Final Thoughts

Real migrations are announced in official channels and almost never require your seed phrase. When a deadline feels urgent, slow down first.

⚠️ Hong Kong SFC flags Hyperliquid as suspicious trading platform, can HYPE price hold $65? 

💭 Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has added decentralized derivatives exchange Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms over concerns that it may be offering services in the jurisdiction without regulatory authorization. The SFC said Hyperliquid was not licensed and was suspected of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong or “actively marketing its services to the Hong Kong public.”

📌 Hyperliquid (HYPE) showed a limited price reaction following the publication of the warning, trading at $68.48 during Thursday’s session, down 0.33% over 24 hours. However, the cryptocurrency remained 12.62% lower over the past month. Hong Kong introduced its licensing framework for centralized virtual asset trading platforms in June 2023, requiring operators conducting business in the city or actively targeting local investors to obtain regulatory authorization.

👀 The commission has previously worked with the Hong Kong Police Force to restrict access to websites associated with suspicious trading platforms. In March 2025, police took steps to block access to Linkbex’s website at the regulator’s request following complaints involving suspected investment fraud. The latest warning against Hyperliquid, however, contains no announcement of an internet service provider block, app-store removal, asset freeze or mandatory suspension of trading services. It does not specifically accuse the platform of fraud.

Kyiv Could Be Days From Unlivable. The Exodus Is Still a Scenario.

Michael Bociurkiw, who runs the World Briefing Report, warns that Kyiv could be days from becoming effectively unlivable, with electricity, water, heating and sewage failing. If that continues, he says, more residents will leave, and "at some point it becomes Europe's problem as well." Forbes ran the warning on Nov. 24.

The piece also cites exodus figures, but they are scenarios, not forecasts. One of them, 20 million, comes from Zelensky's October warning of what could happen if Ukraine fell to Russia. The article itself presents the figures as a sense of scale rather than a prediction.

The evidence from the city is mixed. The Wall Street Journal reports that millions of Ukrainians are reassessing what would make them leave, though many are hunkering down for now. One resident lives on four hours of electricity a day. Another carries water up eight floors. A mother who moved to Lviv in October cited growing fear for her seven-year-old.

The pressure comes from Russian strikes on Kyiv's power, water and sewage systems. A Lawfare dispatch from Kyiv notes that none of the capital's four Soviet-era power plants currently generates electricity. In the first week of November alone, 278 strikes on civilian infrastructure were recorded.

The warning is real, but the exodus is not yet a fact. Some policymakers will cite it to argue for pressing Kyiv to settle. Others will use it to demand more air defense. 

Both camps will point to the same four idle power plants.

📌 Stacks (STX) outlook for 2027: What could drive STX demand? 

🔗 The STX outlook for 2027 will largely depend on growing Bitcoin staking adoption, institutional participation and whether new financial services on Stacks can create sustained demand for the network’s native token. Bitcoin staking already requires participants to commit STX alongside their BTC, while planned developments in lending, trading and network infrastructure could create additional uses for the token. 

🔖 Stacks has started building Bitcoin capital markets through a staking programme that allows holders to earn BTC rewards while committing STX as staking capacity. The first three Bitcoin Bonds have attracted growing interest, with institutional participation from firms including 21shares, UTXO Management, HashKey, Sypher Capital and Bullish.

📊 Beyond staking, STX is used to pay network transaction fees and participate in Stacks’ Proof of Transfer system. Stacks founder and Stacks Labs CEO Muneeb Ali has outlined a longer-term vision that could extend the network’s role into Bitcoin-backed credit, private financial transactions and scalable execution infrastructure.
